whatItDoes: Create a 0.3% sales and use tax throughout Larimer County beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise up to $34.5 million in the first year and amounts based on collections later. Exemptions include groceries for home consumption, gasoline, diapers, prescription drugs and other items exempt by law. Money could fund county purposes, including wildfire and disaster resilience, drinking-water sources, roads, bridges, parks, trails, open space, emergency services, public benefits, justice and other county facilities, and emerging community needs. Revenue would receive an annual independent audit. The county could keep and spend all revenue outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the countywide sales and use tax, annual audit and constitutional revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this sales and use tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Add 0.5 percentage points to Wellington’s sales and use tax beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $995,000 in the first fiscal year and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Money would fund law enforcement and related public-safety services. Revenue above the amount budgeted for those purposes could support other lawful town operations. The town could keep and spend the revenue and investment earnings outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the additional sales and use tax for public safety, use of any excess for other town operations, and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Authorize $28 million in Berthoud debt, with total repayment capped at $60 million, for parks and recreation. Projects could include designing, building and equipping Mountain Vista Park with ballfields, water-recreation features and related improvements. Sales and use tax revenue bonds would be paid from existing town sales and use taxes, without raising taxes. Bond-investment earnings and funds used for repayment would be exempt from Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the parks and recreation borrowing using existing taxes and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not authorize this borrowing or the related revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Extend Johnstown-Milliken School District RE-5J’s existing $4 million annual tax, approved in 2020, beyond its scheduled December 31, 2030 expiration. The measure would impose no new tax. Revenue would go into the general fund for education, including teachers and staff, safety, security and mental-health personnel, career preparation and early-childhood programs. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be collected and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve extending the existing education tax and its revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve extending this tax beyond its existing December 31, 2030 expiration.

whatItDoes: Create Stanley Heights Public Improvement District No. 81 and authorize a property-tax levy no higher than 13.791 mills, with collections beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $48,000 in the first year, with later amounts based on collections. Money would improve and maintain district roads and pay general operating expenses. Property-tax proceeds, vehicle ownership-tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits. The district could also collect and spend amounts above the statutory 5.5% property-tax limit in 2027 and later years.
yesMeans: Approve formation of the district, its property-tax levy and the revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve forming the district or the proposed property tax and revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Create Colland Center Public Improvement District No. 82 and authorize a property-tax levy no higher than 22.942 mills, with collections beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $182,000 in the first year, with later amounts based on collections. Money would improve and maintain district roads and pay general operating expenses. Property-tax proceeds, vehicle ownership-tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits. The district could also collect and spend amounts above the statutory 5.5% property-tax limit in 2027 and later years.
yesMeans: Approve formation of the district, its property-tax levy and the revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve forming the district or the proposed property tax and revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Create Terry Point Estates Public Improvement District No. 85 and authorize a property-tax levy no higher than 26.970 mills, with collections beginning January 1, 2027. It would raise $139,000 in the first year, with later amounts based on collections. Money would improve and maintain district roads and pay general operating expenses. Property-tax proceeds, vehicle ownership-tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits. The district could also collect and spend amounts above the statutory 5.5% property-tax limit in 2027 and later years.
yesMeans: Approve formation of the district, its property-tax levy and the revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve forming the district or the proposed property tax and revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Create an Estes Valley Fire Protection District sales tax of up to 0.5%, starting January 1, 2027. It would raise $3.5 million in the first full fiscal year and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Transactions exempt from state sales taxes, including groceries, would be exempt. Money could fund any lawful district purpose, including wildland-fire equipment and training, fire vehicles, communications and safety equipment, and volunteer-firefighter training and support. Revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside legal revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the district sales tax and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this sales tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Authorize up to $16 million in Thompson Crossing Metropolitan District No. 2 general-obligation bonds, with total repayment capped at $36 million and an effective annual interest rate no higher than 5.25%. Money would finance public improvements, including a new 10-foot-wide paved trail along the district’s southern boundary and lower interest rates on obligations for existing improvements. Bonds would be paid from property taxes voters approved in 2001, without increasing the district’s average property-tax levy for the past ten years. Revenue, investment earnings and bond proceeds would receive a constitutional revenue-limit exception.
yesMeans: Approve the public-improvement borrowing within the stated limits and the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not authorize this borrowing or the related revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Without increasing taxes, waive Poudre Valley Fire Protection District’s 5.25% property-tax limit for all future property-tax years. The district could retain property-tax revenue for staffing, fire and lifesaving equipment, operations and capital needs, and collect, keep and spend district revenue despite other legal revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the permanent waiver and permission to retain and spend district revenue beyond those limits.
noMeans: Do not waive the 5.25% property-tax limit or approve the proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Phase in an additional 4-mill operating property-tax levy for Windsor-Severance Fire Protection District: up to 1.5 mills in 2027, another 1.5 mills in 2031 and another 1 mill in 2034. After all increases, taxes could rise by up to $44,336,787 by tax year 2034, with amounts based on collections in later years. Money would support fire and emergency personnel, vehicles and equipment, service levels, an additional fire station and renovations. Revenue and earnings would have permanent exceptions from Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and applicable statutory limits.
yesMeans: Approve the phased property-tax increases and permanent revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve these phased tax increases or the proposed permanent revenue-limit exceptions.
